question: In the context of Hindu temple architecture, the place where the main idol of a deity is placed is known as _________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Garbhagriha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Garbhagriha**, translating to "womb chamber," is the innermost sanctum of a Hindu temple where the main deity's idol or image is enshrined. It is a sacred and highly significant element of temple architecture.
 
• This chamber is deliberately kept small and dark to create an intimate and spiritual atmosphere, emphasizing the divine presence of the deity.
 
• The **Garbhagriha** is typically located directly under the tallest tower or spire of the temple, known as the **Shikhara** in North Indian temples or the **Vimana** in South Indian temples, symbolizing the connection between earth and the heavens.
 
• Only the priests are allowed to enter the Garbhagriha to perform rituals and offer prayers to the deity. Devotees usually worship from outside the chamber.
 
• The Garbhagriha serves as the primary focus of the temple's design, with other structures like the **Mandapa** (pillared halls) and the temple courtyard designed around it to facilitate congregation and rituals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mandapa:**

 
 
• The **Mandapa** is a pillared hall or pavilion in a Hindu temple, located in front of the Garbhagriha. It serves as a space for devotees to assemble, perform rituals, and listen to spiritual discourses.
 
• Large temples often have multiple Mandapas, each serving different purposes, such as dancing (Natya Mandapa) or marriage ceremonies (Kalyana Mandapa).
 
 
 
• **Shikhara:**
 
 
• The **Shikhara** is the towering spire above the Garbhagriha in North Indian temples. It symbolizes Mount Meru, the mythological sacred mountain at the center of the universe in Hindu cosmology.
 
• The design of the Shikhara varies between regional temple styles, such as the curvilinear Rekha Shikhara of Nagara temples.
 
 
 
• **Vaahan:**
 
 
• The **Vaahan** refers to the mount or vehicle of a deity, often represented as a statue or image positioned in front of the temple or near the deity in the Garbhagriha.
 
• For example, **Nandi**, the bull, serves as the mount of Lord Shiva and is often found facing the Shiva Lingam in Shiva temples.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Temple Architecture:**
 
 
• Hindu temple architecture is deeply symbolic, representing the cosmos and the connection between the physical and spiritual worlds.
 
• The layout and design are based on ancient texts like the **Shilpa Shastras** and reflect the philosophy and beliefs of Hinduism.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Regional Variations:**

 
 
• In North India, temples follow the **Nagara** style, characterized by curvilinear Shikharas and intricate carvings.
 
• In South India, the **Dravidian** style features towering gopurams (entrance gateways) and pyramid-shaped Vimanas.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Famous Temples:**
 
 
• The **Brihadeeswarar Temple** in Tamil Nadu, built by the Chola dynasty, is an excellent example of Dravidian architecture.
 
• The **Khajuraho Temples** in Madhya Pradesh showcase intricate carvings and the Nagara architectural style.
 
 
 
• **Role of Rituals:**
 
 
• Daily worship, festivals, and special rituals are conducted in the temple to honor the deity and involve the community in spiritual practices.
